title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1970-04-15
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > CD > EAC > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a 1970 spring show, highlighted by a scorching Other One/cryptical‑drums jam and flawless band performance.
ai_review.review: The recording is remarkably clean – crisp guitars, balanced vocals and vivid drums make it feel like you’re sitting front row. Musically the night is a tour‑de‑force: the Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → jam → The Other One suite is repeatedly called “smoking,” while Lovelight/NFA/Lovelight, Dancin’ in the Streets, Candyman and Man’s World all receive high praise. Minor drawbacks are only the missing China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider and a cut‑off Hard to Handle, which do not diminish the overall impact.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 70 reviews are 5‑star, lauding both performance and sound quality; only a handful note missing tracks or brief cuts, so the combined show (70 %) + recording (30 %) rating is very high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, clear and well‑balanced; vocals sit perfectly, guitars sparkle, drums punch through. Only occasional criticism for a hard‑to‑handle cut and missing songs, but no noticeable hiss or muddiness.

standout_songs: Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → Jam → The Other One
Lovelight > Not Fade Away > Lovelight sandwich
poor_songs: Missing China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set rides a high‑energy wave with seamless segues—especially the mid‑drums jam into The Other One—and maintains momentum through tight transitions and powerful vocal exchanges, despite a few missing pieces.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for wailing, smoky guitar tone and creative soloing; described as ‘smokin’' and ‘deliberate’.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for grooving bass lines and the “thundering” low end that drives The Other One suite.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned in vocal exchanges during Lovelight/NFA/Lovelight, providing strong rhythm guitar support and occasional lead vocals.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard work (Keith/Brent/Vince) described as solid and occasionally extra personnel added depth; Pigpen’s brief keyboard contribution also highlighted.
band_member_comments.Drums: The percussion is a focal point – the Cryptical > Drums segment, mid‑drums jam and overall tightness are called “smoking,” “intense” and “powerful.”
